claims.content: Ensure that device command safety rules are validated against secured safety rules stored in non-volatile memory before execution, preventing unsafe operations such as opening a gate when another conflicting gate is open.

goal.raw_text: Ensure that device command safety rules are validated against secured safety rules stored in non-volatile memory before execution, preventing unsafe operations such as opening a gate when another conflicting gate is open.

claims.content: System Administrator
The System Administrator must be logged in with a security level and password assigned to their staff member account, as configuration options require authentication for modifying device rules.
The system must be operational and the GUI must be accessible to the System Administrator to display devices, controllers, or workstations that will be affected by rule changes.
An additional login password must be available or entered specifically for configuring device rules, as this option requires extra authentication beyond standard login.
The System Administrator must have access to the Simulator environment to test revised device command safety rules before uploading them to the production system.
A new database version containing the tested rule changes must be prepared and ready for upload after successful testing in the Simulator environment.
The System Administrator logs in and attempts to revise device command safety rules.

trigger.raw_text: The System Administrator logs in and attempts to revise device command safety rules.

claims.content: The System Administrator accesses the configuration screen to modify device command safety rules.
The GUI displays information logs and allows the administrator to view which devices, controllers, or workstations will be affected by the rule changes.
The System Administrator enters an additional login password required specifically for configuring device rules.
The System Administrator revises the device command safety rules within the Simulator environment to test the changes.
After successful testing in the Simulator environment, the System Administrator uploads a new database version containing the revised rules to the production system.
The system updates the secured safety rules stored in non-volatile memory with the new validated rules.
If the GUI analyzes the data before storing in the database and detects conflicting or redundant entries, it shall notify the system administrator.
If a device fails to report completion of the current sequence step within the response time window allotted for the step during a closing sequence, the sequence shall be halted.
If the status for a closure device, which was previously closed at the current entrance, changes to 'unknown' or 'open' during a closing sequence, the sequence shall be halted.

If a 'halted' opening or closing sequence occurs because an offending device status can be corrected within the specified time period, the operator shall be able to enter a 'resume' command to attempt to complete the original sequence.
If the screened command, including any subordinate commands, would result in an unacceptable reversible lanes configuration, the screening check is considered to have failed.
If the system administrator modifies database tables and the GUI analyzes the data before storing it, the GUI shall notify the system administrator of any conflicting or redundant entries.

If a verification failure occurs in checking the non-volatile memory items (where current recomputed 'Message Digest' values do not correspond with 'record' values), the system shall prevent the affected unit from being used in control sequences.
The new database version containing the revised device command safety rules is uploaded to the production system.
The secured safety rules stored in non-volatile memory are updated with the validated rule changes.
A UTC date/time stamp is updated as the last step in the process which builds the time stamped code/data section for the modified Control Unit Non-Volatile Memory items.

A table of returned 'one-way hash function' (Message Digest) values, stored as hexadecimal characters, is produced and maintained in non-volatile memory for each Control Unit Non-Volatile Memory item that was created or modified.
